Cross-validation of the conditional average treatment effect (CATE) score

Source: R/crossv.R
catecv.Rd

Provides doubly robust estimation of average treatment effects for binary, count, and survival outcomes in nested and mutually exclusive subgroups of patients defined by an estimated conditional average treatment effect (CATE) score via cross-validation (CV).

Usage

catecv(
  response,
  data,
  outcome_model,
  outcome_method = NULL,
  benefit_model = NULL,
  benefit_method = "t_learner",
  ps_model,
  ps_method = "glm",
  censoring_model = NULL,
  censoring_method = "breslow",
  minPS = 0.01,
  maxPS = 0.99,
  followup.time = NULL,
  tau0 = NULL,
  higher.y = TRUE,
  prop.cutoff = seq(0.5, 1, length = 6),
  prop.multi = c(0, 1/3, 2/3, 1),
  abc = TRUE,
  train.prop = 3/4,
  cv.n = 10,
  error.max = 0.1,
  max.iter = 5000,
  surv.min = 0.025,
  xvar.smooth.score = NULL,
  xvar.smooth.init = NULL,
  tree.depth = 2,
  n.trees.rf = 1000,
  n.trees.boosting = 200,
  B = 3,
  Kfold = 5,
  error.maxNR = 0.001,
  max.iterNR = 150,
  tune = c(0.5, 2),
  seed = NULL,
  plot.gbmperf = FALSE,
  verbose = 0,
  contrast.control = list(),
  rmst.control = list(),
  ps.control = list(),
  rf.control = list(),
  ...,
  xvar.smooth = NULL
)

Arguments

response

A string describing the type of outcome in the data. Allowed values include "binary", "count" (see catecvcount()), "survival" (see catecvsurv()). Continuous outcomes are not implemented.

data

A data frame containing the variables in the outcome, treatment, and censoring models (if specified); a data frame with n rows (1 row per observation).

outcome_model

A formula specifying the outcome and baseline covariates. Use a Surv response for survival and include an exposure offset for count outcomes.

outcome_method

Outcome-model method for each benefit_method. The default for a T-learner is 'logistic' for binary, 'poisson' for count, and 'coxph' for survival outcomes. Supply the method for each doubly robust score explicitly.

benefit_model

Optional one-sided formula for the covariates and terms used in two-regression and contrast-regression scores. The default uses the terms in outcome_model. T-learners use outcome_model directly.

benefit_method

Score-construction method, with one entry per outcome_method. The default is 't_learner'. See catefit for supported combinations.

ps_model

A formula for the treatment model, with treatment on the left. It estimates propensity scores. For a common randomization probability, use an intercept-only formula such as trt ~ 1.

ps_method

Treatment-model fitting method. The default 'glm' uses logistic regression. 'lasso' uses a logistic model with LASSO screening for two-way interactions.

censoring_model

Survival only. A one-sided formula for the model that estimates probabilities of remaining uncensored for inverse probability of censoring weighting (IPCW). The default uses the outcome-model covariates and treatment.

censoring_method

Survival only. 'breslow' (default) uses Cox regression with the Breslow estimator. Accelerated failure time options are 'aft (exponential)', 'aft (weibull)', 'aft (lognormal)', and 'aft (loglogistic)'.

minPS

A numerical value (in `[0, 1]`) below which estimated propensity scores should be truncated. Default is 0.01.

maxPS

A numerical value (in `(0, 1]`) above which estimated propensity scores should be truncated. Must be strictly greater than minPS. Default is 0.99.

followup.time

A column name in data specifying the maximum follow-up time, interpreted as the potential censoring time. Only applies for survival outcomes. Default is NULL, which corresponds to unknown potential censoring time.

tau0

The truncation time for defining restricted mean time lost. Only applies for survival outcomes. Default is NULL, which corresponds to setting the truncation time as the maximum survival time in the data.

higher.y

A logical value indicating whether higher (TRUE) or lower (FALSE) values of the outcome are more desirable. Default is TRUE.

prop.cutoff

A vector of numerical values (in `(0, 1]`) specifying percentiles of the estimated CATE scores to define nested subgroups. Each element represents the cutoff to separate observations in nested subgroups (below vs above cutoff). The length of prop.cutoff is the number of nested subgroups. An equally-spaced sequence of proportions ending with 1 is recommended. Default is seq(0.5, 1, length = 6).

prop.multi

A vector of numerical values (in `[0, 1]`) specifying percentiles of the estimated CATE scores to define mutually exclusive subgroups. It should start with 0, end with 1, and be of length(prop.multi) > 2. Each element represents the cutoff to separate the observations into length(prop.multi) - 1 mutually exclusive subgroups. Default is c(0, 1/3, 2/3, 1).

abc

A logical value indicating whether the area between curves (ABC) should be calculated at each cross-validation iterations, for each scoring method. Default is TRUE. Binary ABC requires at least two distinct prop.cutoff values.

train.prop

A numerical value (in `(0, 1)`) indicating the proportion of total data used for training. Default is 3/4.

cv.n

A positive integer value indicating the number of cross-validation iterations. Default is 10.

error.max

A numerical value > 0 indicating the tolerance (maximum value of error) for the largest standardized absolute difference in the covariate distributions or in the doubly robust estimated rate ratios between the training and validation sets. This is used to define a balanced training-validation splitting. Default is 0.1. Not available for binary outcomes, which use treatment-stratified random splits.

max.iter

A positive integer value indicating the maximum number of iterations when searching for a balanced training-validation split. Default is 5,000. Not available for binary outcomes.

surv.min

Lower bound for the estimated probability of remaining uncensored. Defaults to 0.025.

xvar.smooth.score

Reserved for continuous-outcome scores.

xvar.smooth.init

Names of outcome-model variables to smooth for count GAMs. Equivalent to xvar.smooth for count outcomes.

tree.depth

Maximum depth of boosting trees. Defaults to 2.

n.trees.rf

Number of trees for survival random forests. Defaults to 1000.

n.trees.boosting

Maximum number of trees for boosting. Defaults to 200.

B

Number of cross-fitting repetitions used by two-regression and contrast regression. Defaults to 3.

Kfold

Number of folds used for cross-fitting within each training set. Defaults to 5.

error.maxNR

Newton–Raphson convergence tolerance for contrast regression. Defaults to 0.001.

max.iterNR

Maximum number of Newton–Raphson iterations for contrast regression. Defaults to 150.

tune

Two positive Newton–Raphson tuning values for contrast regression. Defaults to c(0.5, 2).

seed

An optional integer specifying an initial randomization seed for reproducibility. Default is NULL, corresponding to no seed.

plot.gbmperf

Whether to plot boosting performance. Defaults to FALSE.

verbose

An integer value indicating what kind of intermediate progress messages should be printed. 0 means no outputs. 1 means only progress bar and run time. 2 means progress bar, run time, and all errors and warnings. Default is 0.

contrast.control

A named list of options for count or survival contrast regression. Supported names are solver ("C", the default, or "R"), error.maxNR, max.iterNR, tune, and optim.control (a named list passed to stats::optim on fallback). List entries override the corresponding top-level NR arguments. Options are kept separate from ..., which is forwarded to boosting. Count and survival outcomes support this list; continuous outcomes retain their existing solver.

rmst.control

Named options for Cox restricted mean survival integration. Supported entry: solver = "C" (default) or solver = "R". The C backend accumulates each patient's integral without allocating a patient-by-event-time matrix. Cox model fitting is unchanged. Available only for survival outcomes; independent of contrast.control.

ps.control

Named options for LASSO propensity-score interaction screening. Supported entry: solver = "C" (default) or solver = "R". Only affects screening when ps_method = "lasso"; the LASSO fit and interaction selection rule are unchanged. Kept separate from boosting's ... and other numerical controls.

rf.control

Named list of randomForestSRC options: mtry, nodesize, nsplit, nodedepth, and splitrule. Applies to both treatment arms and survival initial-predictor forests. Use n.trees.rf for the number of trees.

...

Additional arguments. Deprecated argument names from precmed 1.1.0 remain supported for backward compatibility and emit warnings.

xvar.smooth

Names of variables used as smooth terms for count GAM outcome models. By default, all eligible outcome-model variables are used.

Value

For binary response, a "precmed" object with one ate.* list per method, containing matrices of training and validation risk differences for nested high and low subgroups and mutually exclusive groups, with one column per iteration, and abc.valid when requested. It also contains overall training and validation effects, props, splits (row indices), subgroup.support, and messages accessible with diagnostics(). For count response, see description of outputs in catecvcount(). For survival response, see description of outputs in catecvsurv().

Details

Each iteration fits scores on the training split using the same score-fitting routines as catefit. The fitted score is applied to the held-out split before its subgroup effects are estimated.

For binary outcomes, each iteration randomly splits each treatment arm into training and validation sets. The score is fitted on training data only and applied to both sets. Percentile cutoffs are calculated separately in each set using its scores, without using validation outcomes. Ties may make nested groups larger than their nominal proportions. Mutually exclusive groups use half-open intervals, with the last interval including its upper endpoint; tied cutoffs can produce empty groups. Subgroup risk differences are estimated separately in each set using an augmented inverse-propensity estimator. Score-fitting or subgroup failures return NA with a warning and recorded diagnostics; ABC is NA if any required estimate is unavailable. ABC integrates the validation risk-difference curve minus the overall validation effect, reversing the sign when lower outcomes are desirable. These subgroup comparisons assess ranking, not calibration; causal interpretation requires exchangeability, positivity, consistency, and appropriate nuisance-model assumptions. error.max and max.iter are not supported for binary splits. The binary score methods are described in catefit(). For count response, see details in catecvcount(). For survival response, see details in catecvsurv().

catefit() function and boxplot(), abc methods for "precmed" objects.

Examples

# \donttest{
cate_1 <- catecv(response = "count",
                 data = countExample,
                 outcome_method = "poisson",
                 outcome_model = y ~ age + female + previous_treatment +
                              previous_cost + previous_number_relapses +
                              offset(log(years)),
                 ps_model = trt ~ age + previous_treatment,
                 higher.y = FALSE, cv.n = 5, seed = 999, verbose = 1)
#> Variable trt was recoded to 0/1 with drug0->0 and drug1->1.
#> 
  |                                                                            
  |                                                                      |   0%
#> cv = 1 
#>   splitting the data..
#>   training..
#>   validating..
#> 
#> cv = 2 
#>   splitting the data..
#>   training..
#>   validating..
#> 
#> cv = 3 
#>   splitting the data..
#>   training..
#>   validating..
#> 
#> cv = 4 
#>   splitting the data..
#>   training..
#>   validating..
#> 
#> cv = 5 
#>   splitting the data..
#>   training..
#>   validating..
#> 
#> Total runtime : 8.64 secs 

plot(cate_1, ylab = "RMTL ratio of drug1 vs drug0 in each subgroup")

boxplot(cate_1, ylab = "RMTL ratio of drug1 vs drug0 in each subgroup")

abc(cate_1)
#>               cv1       cv2       cv3        cv4       cv5
#> poisson 0.1375899 0.1172791 0.1120313 0.06136285 0.1877103

# Survival outcome
library(survival)
tau0 <- with(survivalExample,
             min(quantile(y[trt == "drug1"], 0.95), quantile(y[trt == "drug0"], 0.95)))

cate_2 <- catecv(response = "survival",
                 data = survivalExample,
                 outcome_method = c("poisson", "random_forest"),
                 benefit_method = rep("t_learner", 2),
                 outcome_model = Surv(y, d) ~ age + female + previous_cost +
                              previous_number_relapses,
                 ps_model = trt ~ age + previous_treatment,
                 censoring_model = ~ age + previous_cost + previous_treatment,
                 tau0 = tau0,
                 higher.y = TRUE,
                 surv.min = 0.025,
                 cv.n = 5,
                 seed = 999)
#> Variable trt was recoded to 0/1 with drug0->0 and drug1->1.

plot(cate_2, ylab = "RMTL ratio of drug1 vs drug0 in each subgroup")

boxplot(cate_2, ylab = "RMTL ratio of drug1 vs drug0 in each subgroup")
#> Warning: Removed 10 rows containing non-finite outside the scale range
#> (`stat_boxplot()`).

abc(cate_2)
#>                    cv1       cv2       cv3       cv4        cv5
#> poisson      0.2165482 0.2183456 0.1012403 0.2153617 0.09806659
#> randomForest 0.2252653 0.2063741 0.1461175 0.2431729 0.15440263

# }
